Toddler and Preschool Nutrition
After the rapid growth spurt of the first year of life, the normal decrease in food 
intake of 2 year-olds associated with a slowed growth rate may cause concern in unin-
formed parents. Toddlers’ intake will vary depending on the timing of their growth 
spurts. In order to meet the nutritional needs of children between 2 and 5 years of age, 
small nutrient-rich meals and snacks are needed. It is recommended that a small 
snack be given between each meal and at bedtime. Parents need to know that a smaller 
appetite, varying from day to day, is normal for children at this age.
Portion Sizes for Toddlers
My Plate provides excellent guidance regarding portion sizes of all foods and a wealth 
of information on meal planning for people of all ages, based on age, sex, and activity 
level.21 For toddlers, it provides an interactive tool that allows parents and clinicians 
to estimate calorie needs based on physical activity level. These calorie needs are 
then used to choose the appropriate sample meal plan based on a specific number 
of ­serving sizes for each food group. Sample menus are also available for a range of 
calorie levels.
